text:
Predicates:
TransportMultiple(x) ::: x can transport multiple passengers.
OneSeater(x) ::: x is a one-seater.
TeslaModel3(x) ::: x is a Tesla Model 3.
SingleSeatElectricCar(x) ::: x is a single-seat electric car.
SoloEV(x) ::: x is a Solo EV car.
JohnsCar(x) ::: x is John's car.

Premises:
∀x (TransportMultiple(x) → ¬OneSeater(x)) ::: If something can transport multiple passengers, then it is not a one-seater.
∀x (TeslaModel3(x) → TransportMultiple(x)) ::: All Tesla Model 3 can transport multiple passengers.
∀x (SingleSeatElectricCar(x) → OneSeater(x)) ::: All single-seat electric cars are one-seaters.
∀x (SoloEV(x) → SingleSeatElectricCar(x)) ::: All Solo EV cars are single-seat electric cars.
∃x (JohnsCar(x) ∧ ¬TeslaModel3(x)) → ∀x (JohnsCar(x) → (¬TeslaModel3(x) ∨ SingleSeatElectricCar(x))) ::: If John's car is not a Tesla Model 3, then John's car is not a Tesla Model 3 or a single-seat electric car.

Conclusion:
∃x (JohnsCar(x) ∧ TeslaModel3(x)) ::: John's car is a Tesla Model 3.
